BIOS 410.description: Statistical modeling, primarily using applications in public health. Measures of agreement, principles of statistical inference, correlation, simple and multiple linear regression, categorical independent variables, interaction, repeated measures, and logistic regression.
BIOS 410.subject: BIOS
BIOS 410.title: Introduction to Biostatistical Modeling

BIOS 490.description: Enrollment and topic to be approved in advance by advisor and instructor. May be repeated.
BIOS 490.subject: BIOS
BIOS 490.title: Independent Study

BIOS 700.description: Health-related statistical applications. Descriptive statistics, probability, confidence intervals, hypothesis testing, regression, correlation, ANOVA. May not be used as part of a degree program in epidemiology or biostatistics. Three lecture hours and one laboratory hour per week.
BIOS 700.subject: BIOS
BIOS 700.title: Introduction to Biostatistics

BIOS 701.description: Descriptive and inferential statistical applications to public health. Probability, interval estimation, hypothesis testing, measures of association. Three lecture hours and one laboratory hour per week. Intended for those who will be involved in research applications of biostatistics.
BIOS 701.subject: BIOS
BIOS 701.title: Concepts and Methods of Biostatistics

BIOS 709.description: Working with public health data using statistical software. Effective ways to store, clean, merge, and format public health data for analysis.
BIOS 709.subject: BIOS
BIOS 709.title: Basic Software for Public Health

BIOS 710.description: Statistical data management techniques. Microcomputer applications, communication between microcomputers and mainframe, tape and disk storage, access of large health-related databases.
BIOS 710.subject: BIOS
BIOS 710.title: Effective Data Management for Public Health

BIOS 711.description: Students will learn the software program R for performing data management. The course covers basic to advanced commands for properly formatting output, merging data, working with functions, graphing, using programming loops for preparing data for analysis for public health data.
BIOS 711.subject: BIOS
BIOS 711.title: Introduction to R Programming

BIOS 712.description: Students will learn the software program Stata for performing data management. The course covers basic to advanced commands for properly formatting output, merging data, working with functions, graphing, using programming loops for preparing data for analysis for public health data.
BIOS 712.subject: BIOS
BIOS 712.title: Introduction to Stata Software

BIOS 714.description: This course focuses the uses of Microsoft Access for data management in public health. The course takes the student through building tables, forms, queries, reports and finishes with automated scripts for each of use with Access.
BIOS 714.subject: BIOS
BIOS 714.title: Introduction to MS Access for Public Health

BIOS 719.description: This course focuses on advanced programming for managing and analyzing data using SAS. Building upon skills learned in BIOS 709 (Introduction to SAS), students will learn data management using PROC SQL . Students will also become familiar with the SAS Macro Language which prepares data for conducting efficient statistical analysis.
BIOS 719.subject: BIOS
BIOS 719.title: Advanced SAS Methods for Public Health

BIOS 720.description: This course teaches advanced techniques for creating and using large data sets. Students will learn advanced techniques for working with data, cleaning data, and preparing it for analysis using three software packages (SAS, STATA, MS Access) for data entry, data management, and presentation. For statistical analysis, students will learn advanced SAS, the primary statistical package used for data analysis in other biostatistics and epidemiology courses.
BIOS 720.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: C or better in BIOS 710.
BIOS 720.subject: BIOS
BIOS 720.title: Advanced Data Management in Public Health

BIOS 735.description: This course introduces the fundamental concepts and applications of machine learning (ML) in the context of public health, biostatistics, and related fields (e.g., epidemiology, psychology, neuroscience, genetics). Students will learn how to prepare data, select and implement appropriate machine learning methods, and evaluate model performance—all using R. Emphasis will be placed on conceptual understanding, practical implementation, and interpretation of results rather than on mathematical derivations. By the end of the course, students will be prepared to incorporate ML techniques into their own research projects, with a special focus on the unique challenges and ethical considerations inherent in analyzing public health data.
BIOS 735.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: B or better in BIOS 757and BIOS 755 or equivalent.
BIOS 735.subject: BIOS
BIOS 735.title: Machine Learning for Public Health Applications

BIOS 745.description: Analysis of current and prospective issues in biostatistics, including historical foundations. Includes student exploration of unsolved problems and examination of central issues in biostatistics.
BIOS 745.subject: BIOS
BIOS 745.title: Seminar in Biostatistics

BIOS 746.description: Students will learn the basics of data collection methods, sampling design for linear, logistic, and survival analysis complex models using survey data. Students will also learn about weight adjustments, imputation methods with an emphasis on both applied models and the theory behind them.
BIOS 746.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: B or better in STAT 512 and STAT 513 or equivalent.
BIOS 746.subject: BIOS
BIOS 746.title: Introduction to Complex Survey Data Analysis

BIOS 753.description: Process, skills, and management of undertaking health studies in the human community.
BIOS 753.subject: BIOS
BIOS 753.title: Community Health Studies

BIOS 754.description: Analysis of discrete data in public health studies. Relative risk, odds ratio, rates and proportions, contingency tables, logistic regression, introduction to other advanced topics. Not for biostatistics majors.
BIOS 754.subject: BIOS
BIOS 754.title: Discrete Data Analysis

BIOS 755.description: Introduction to principles and methods for longitudinal multi-level modeling. Focus on data analysis and interpretation.
BIOS 755.subject: BIOS
BIOS 755.title: Introduction to Longitudinal Data Analysis

BIOS 757.description: Public health applications of correlation, regression, multiple regression, single and multi-factor analysis of variance and analysis of covariance.
BIOS 757.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: a course in introductory statistics.
BIOS 757.subject: BIOS
BIOS 757.title: Intermediate Biostatistics

BIOS 758.description: Public health applications of correlation, regression, multiple regression, single and multi-factor analysis of variance and analysis of covariance. Additional topics in analysis of health data including regression diagnostics, multi-collinearity of observational data, ridge/nonlinear regression, principal components, random/mixed effects, unbalanced designs, repeated measures and sampling and design effects.
BIOS 758.subject: BIOS
BIOS 758.title: Advanced Linear Models in Biostatistics

BIOS 759.description: The concepts, principles, and biostatistical techniques necessary to analyze categorical epidemiological data including dose response curves, life tables, and discrete measures of association. Estimation of parameters for logistic and other commonly used epidemiological models.
BIOS 759.subject: BIOS
BIOS 759.title: Theory and Methods of Discrete Data Analysis

BIOS 760.description: The basic and advanced statistical techniques necessary for the design, conduct, analysis, and interpretation of results of clinical trials.
BIOS 760.subject: BIOS
BIOS 760.title: Biostatistical Methods in Clinical Trials

BIOS 761.description: Methods for the analysis of survival data in the biomedical setting. Underlying concepts; standard parametric and nonparametric methods for one or several samples; concomitant variables and the proportional hazards model.
BIOS 761.subject: BIOS
BIOS 761.title: Survival Analysis

BIOS 762.description: This course is an introduction to important topics and key concepts in statistical genetics, with emphasis on statistics methods and their applications to human complex diseases. The course will cover major concepts and classical statistical methods for the analysis of family and population based human genetic data.
BIOS 762.subject: BIOS
BIOS 762.title: Biostatistical Modeling of Genomic Data

BIOS 765.description: Fundamentals of constructing, analyzing, and interpreting biomedical studies; internal and external validity, sample size determination, completely random designs, blocking crossover designs, factorial designs, confounding, nested designs, repeated measure designs.
BIOS 765.subject: BIOS
BIOS 765.title: Research Design in the Biomedical Sciences

BIOS 767.description: Spatial statistics methods commonly used in public health including mapping, tests for spatial correlation, hypothesis tests for spatial clustering, and regression models with spatial random effects.
BIOS 767.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: B or better in BIOS 700 or BIOS 701.
BIOS 767.subject: BIOS
BIOS 767.title: Spatial Statistics for Public Health

BIOS 770.description: Modern methods for the analysis of repeated measures, correlated outcomes, and longitudinal data, including repeated measures ANOVA, generalized linear models, random effects, and generalized estimating equations.
BIOS 770.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: BIOS 757 or BIOS 758 or STAT 701 or STAT 705.
BIOS 770.subject: BIOS
BIOS 770.title: Applied Longitudinal Data Analysis

BIOS 772.description: Introduces deep learning architectures for analyzing large-scale biomedical data including genomics, electronic health records, and medical imaging, emphasizing model interpretability, ethical considerations, multi-modal data integration with real-world example applications, and implementation using Python.
BIOS 772.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: B or better in BIOS 757.
BIOS 772.subject: BIOS
BIOS 772.title: Artificial intelligence for Biomedical Data

BIOS 775.description: Bioinformatics analyses related to public health and biomedical research. Gene-gene and gene-environment interaction, phylogeny analysis in disease classification, and clustering for expression data. Data analyses, simulation studies, algorithms, and interpretation of health data.
BIOS 775.subject: BIOS
BIOS 775.title: Biostatistical Aspects of Bioinformatics

BIOS 780.description: Principles and methods of quantile regression, a robust and distribution-free statistical approach that extends the classical mean regression to the analysis of complex treatment effects.
BIOS 780.subject: BIOS
BIOS 780.title: Introduction to Quantile Regression

BIOS 790.description: Directed research on a topic to be developed by M.P.H. or M.S.P.H. student and instructor. May be repeated.
BIOS 790.subject: BIOS
BIOS 790.title: Independent Study

BIOS 794.description: Content varies by title. Course may be repeated for a total of 6 credit hours.
BIOS 794.subject: BIOS
BIOS 794.title: Selected Topics in Biostatistics

BIOS 811.description: Parametric survival analysis, accelerated failure time model, frailty model, competing risk mode and multi-state model. Techniques motivated by applications in epidemiology and clinical medicine research, applications demonstrated using public health data sets.
BIOS 811.subject: BIOS
BIOS 811.title: Survival Analysis II

BIOS 815.description: Statistical theory and applications extending regression and analysis of variance to non-normal data. An integrated treatment encompassing logistic and other binary regressions, log-linear models, and gamma regression models.
BIOS 815.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: STAT 713 or STAT 513 and STAT 705 or BIOS 757.
BIOS 815.subject: BIOS
BIOS 815.title: Generalized Linear Models

BIOS 816.description: R is a free and open source software environment for statistical computing and graphics. This course provides the principles and techniques to efficiently design, implement, and execute simulation and data analysis routines in quantitative fields like biostatistics, statistics, engineering, finance, and data science.
BIOS 816.subject: BIOS
BIOS 816.title: Advanced R Programming in Public Health

BIOS 818.description: An overview of advanced computational statistics for signal and network analysis with a wide variety of social, genomic and neuroscientific applications. All course modules include a hands-on component.
BIOS 818.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: B or better in BIOS 701, BIOS 757, BIOS 711, STAT 512 and STAT 513.
BIOS 818.subject: BIOS
BIOS 818.title: Advanced Computational Statistics for Signal and Network Analysis

BIOS 820.description: Bayesian statistical methods including hierarchical modeling and the use of the Markov Chane Monte Carlo (MCMC) methods.
BIOS 820.subject: BIOS
BIOS 820.title: Bayesian Biostatistics and Computation

BIOS 822.description: A comprehensive introduction to the statistical methods used in the analysis of geo-referenced spatial health data. Topics range from disease mapping to prospective surveillance.
BIOS 822.subject: BIOS
BIOS 822.title: Statistical Methods in Spatial Epidemiology

BIOS 825.description: Analysis of multivariate data as found in biomedical studies: multivariate linear models, principal component analysis, factor analysis, discriminant and cluster analysis. Other special multivariate topics such as principal component regression.
BIOS 825.subject: BIOS
BIOS 825.title: Multivariate Biostatistics

BIOS 835.description: The focus of this course will be on using biostatistical models to predict and provide information on complex public health datasets. We will focus more on prediction of outcome(s) than estimation of the impact of a risk factor. However, some interferential methods for risk factors will be reviewed and (for all methods) techniques to measure variable importance will be discussed. Further, unsupervised learning methods (e.g., clustering) will be discussed. Prediction and predictive inference will be main themes in the course along with learning how to implement the methods in R software. See the syllabus course schedule for a full list of topics.
BIOS 835.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: B or better in BIOS 770 or equivalent.
BIOS 835.subject: BIOS
BIOS 835.title: Biostatistical Machine Learning for Public Health

BIOS 845.prerequisite_text: Prerequisites: complete at least one semester of course work and consent of instructor.
BIOS 845.subject: BIOS
BIOS 845.title: Doctoral Seminar

BIOS 850.description: Threshold, mass action and target theory; empirical dose response functions; methods in current use among health science researchers.
BIOS 850.subject: BIOS
BIOS 850.title: Binary Dose Response Theory and Methods

BIOS 890.description: Directed research on a topic to be developed by doctoral student and instructor. May be repeated.
BIOS 890.subject: BIOS
BIOS 890.title: Independent Study

BIOS 894.description: Discussion on current and emerging issues in biostatistics.
BIOS 894.subject: BIOS
BIOS 894.title: Selected Topics in Biostatistics

BIOS 898.description: Students are required to conduct applied public health methods and strategies as a part of their practicum experience. In particular, the student should successfully implement and interpret the results of biostatistical methods in the organization.
BIOS 898.subject: BIOS
BIOS 898.title: Doctor of Public Health Practicum

BIOS 899.description: Prerequisite: one full year (18 hours) of graduate study beyond the master’s level.
BIOS 899.subject: BIOS
BIOS 899.title: Dissertation Preparation
